title: Assessment of Global Brain Atrophy and Specific Brain Regions in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis
summary: In people with multiple sclerosis (MS), loss of brain volume often occurs over the course of the disease. This loss can begin early and is linked to problems such as memory difficulties, fatigue, and physical limitations. This study aims to investigate how the MS medication cladribine affects the loss of brain volume, compared to other MS medications. To do this, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans that were already taken as part of regular medical care will be used. These images will be analyzed with special computer software that measures the size of different brain regions. In addition, information from patients' medical records will be used, such as age, sex, and disease course. This is a retrospective study, meaning only existing data and images will be used. No additional examinations, risks, or effort will result for the participants.
conditions: Multiple sclerosis (MS), a chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system characterized by progressive loss of brain volume (brain atrophy).

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of MS patients (≥ 18 years, confirmed MS diagnosis according to the 2025 McDonald criteria) treated with cladribine. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
MRI data from adult patients (≥18 years) with a confirmed diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) according to the 2025 McDonald criteria receiving treatment with cladribine.
Exclusion criteria:
MS patients who underwent only a single MRI examination. MS patients for whom no MPRAGE sequence (3D T1-weighted imaging) was acquired. MS patients whose MRI scans were deemed to be of insufficient image quality for analysis.
